title: Standardize VPC health probes and SLO-driven alerts for private deployments
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Private (VPC) deployments currently rely on an ad-hoc set of probes (kube readiness/liveness and a few HTTP endpoints) across customer environments. There is no standardized SLO definition or Terraform IaC module that codifies probe endpoints, metrics ingestion, or alert thresholds. This causes inconsistent behavior between customers (some have noisy false positives; others never alert until customer impact), and makes upgrades/runtimes changes risky.
acceptance_criteria: - A Terraform module (v1) that injects standardized Kubernetes liveness/readiness and a small sidecar HTTP probe for runtime-level checks into Redwood Private helm charts.
implementation_steps: Define probe endpoints and payloads: /healthz (ok|degraded|fail), /ready for readiness, /metrics/probe-status for detailed token throughput and kv-cache stats

Design SLOs: 99.9% latency p95 & p99 targets per-route, error rate <0.25% per-minute for 1m windows, saturation thresholds per-GPU >85% triggers alert, token throughput drop of >30% vs baseline triggers degradation alert
Create Terraform module private_probe_v1 with variables: probe_path, initial_delay, period_seconds, failure_threshold, telemetry_labels
Emitter: wire probe events to Prometheus exporter; ensure private deployments can forward to customer or Redwood-managed Datadog/Prometheus via configurable remote_write
Add alerts in alertmanager/Datadog: SLO burn-rate alert, latency SLO violation, rising 5xx rate, sustained low token throughput
Integrate with Console: display SLO status per-customer and per-deployment in Private Console UI (dashboard tile)
Add migration path and compatibility toggles for existing customers (opt-in initial rollout, then opt-out window)
Document runbooks and automated rollback gates (canary probe checks before upgrade)
testing_plan: Unit tests for Terraform module and Helm hook templates
E2E on staging: deploy private stack with module enabled, simulate traffic patterns: normal, burst, slow tokens, backend errors
Chaos tests: kill a worker pod to validate saturation alerts and autoscaler reaction
Load tests to establish baselines for token throughput per GPU family (A100, H100, L4) and publish fixtures to infra repository
monitoring_and_alerts: Probes emit metrics: probe_status{status=(ok|degraded|fail)}, probe_latency_seconds (histogram), probe_5xx_count, probe_token_throughput_per_sec, gpu_utilization_percent. SLOs mapped to these metrics: latency p95 < 120ms (hosted baseline may be lower for private), error_rate <0.25%, saturation >85% is warning, >95% critical, token throughput 30th percentile above baseline. Alerts: - warning on sustained burn-rate 1.5x for 30m - critical on burn-rate 3x for 5m - immediate critical on probe_status==fail for >2 minutes
notes: Trade-offs: pushing too many checks into liveness can cause restart loops; we prefer a small fast liveness and a richer readiness/sidecar that performs deeper runtime checks
We chose a separate /metrics/probe-status endpoint to avoid inflating main /metrics scrape and to expose token-throughput counters with labels for model, seq_len, and quantization profile
Plan to ship Terraform module as opt-in v1 for 30 days to gather field telemetry before defaulting to on for all new private installs
